dataset_title: MBMA Cold-Formed C- and Z-Purlin Roof System Test Programs (1975-2000): Pooled Full-Scale, Component and Material Data

derivations.note: Test-to-predicted ratio is by definition the measured failure load divided by the predicted (AISI/base-test) failure load, both in plf for the same test; fill only where the paper does not print the ratio.

The base test reduction factor R is defined as the measured base-test failure moment divided by the theoretical (fully braced AISI) flexural capacity of the same section, R = Mus/Mnt; exact by definition when both are in the same moment unit.
Where a paper prints R only as a percentage (MBMA_9002 r_percent), the fraction is the percentage divided by 100; a pure unit conversion, exact by definition.
1 kip-ft = 12 kip-in; pure unit conversion, exact by definition. Used for MBMA_9610, which prints M_t in k-ft. (hand edit 2026-11-10, Cris Moen review)

groups.description: Single-span, simply supported, two-purlin-line standing seam roof assemblies loaded to failure by vacuum chamber (gravity), i.e. AISI base tests, all reporting a failure load per purlin line and, mostly, a base-test reduction factor R.

constants.evidence: Table S1 header note: 'Purlin spacing was 5 ft o.c. with 1 ft deck overhang in all tests'

members.note: 118 base tests; failure_load_as_printed is the Total Applied Load and INCLUDES deck (4.00 plf) and purlin self weight, unlike most other papers whose loads are applied load only.

constants.evidence: Table S1 header note: 'Tributary width per purlin line is 5 ft. (purlin spacing).'

members.note: 17 base tests, Series I-IV; includes both Z and 9 in. C purlins. R is printed as a percentage (r_percent), hence mapped to base_test_r_percent. Table 3.1 join by test_identification is imperfect because several labels are printed inconsistently (e.g. R-F-9C0.075-20 vs P-F-9C0.075-20); unmatched rows should be left blank, not guessed.
Nine single-span base tests (test_id ending -1) of Z and C purlins with rib/pan standing seam panels; the matching three-span confirming tests go to the multi-span group.

15 single-span standing seam base tests (Fisher and Nunnery 1996): 93-1 to 93-8 purlins facing the same direction, 94-1 to 94-7 opposed. failure_load_plf is W(tot), the line load on one purlin line (M_t = W L^2/8). base_test_r is the printed M_t/M_n, which excludes the overturning moment from anchorage forces (p.3). F_y is 55 ksi (apparently nominal) for the 93 tests and varies for the 94 tests. failure_pressure_psf (Table 4) exists only for 93-1 to 93-8. Dead-load treatment is not stated. (hand edit 2026-11-10, Cris Moen review)

groups.name: Single-span standing seam roof base tests under gravity loading

groups.description: Standard ASTM tensile coupons cut from purlin (and in some reports sheet/panel) material of the test specimens, all reporting coupon dimensions, yield stress, ultimate strength and elongation.

members.note: 32 coupons, two per test (East/West); the printed last row is an average of all 32 and must be dropped by the program (it carries no test number). The printed 'Avg.' row is now removed by a row filter (hand edit 2026-11-10); it had been pooled as a coupon.

constants.evidence: Table 3.1 note: 'Coupons were taken from the web area of representative purlins used in each test.'

members.note: One averaged coupon result per test; no coupon width reported. Z-R-P/S-1 yield (62.45 ksi) conflicts with the appendix sheet (67.45 ksi).

constants.evidence: Table 4.5 note: 'Coupons were taken from the web area of the failed purlin in each base test.'

members.note: 17 coupons, one per base test; several printed thicknesses disagree with the thickness implied by the test label.

constants.evidence: Table 3.1 content line: 'Measured tensile coupon properties of material cut from the web of a failed purlin in each test.'

members.note: One averaged coupon per test; I.P. Test 3 Z-TF has no coupon (yield assumed), with blank strength and elongation.

groups.name: Tensile coupon tests of purlin and panel steel

groups.description: Per-purlin measured cross-section dimensions (depth, thickness, flange widths, lip lengths, bend radii and lip angles) recorded with the same measurement scheme and figure nomenclature in three Murray-era reports.

constants.evidence: Table 2.1 title: 'Measured cross-section dimensions of the two interior (test) 9x3 C-purlins used in each of the sixteen tests.'

groups.name: Measured purlin cross-section geometry, per purlin line

groups.description: AISI effective-section analyses computed from the measured dimensions of each test purlin, giving gross and effective section properties, element-governed allowable moments, the predicted uniform failure load and the computed deflection per 100 plf.

constants.evidence: Table 2.2 description: 'based on measured dimensions and an assumed yield stress of 56 ksi'; span 25 ft 0 in. except Tests 15 and 16

groups.name: AISI computed section properties and predicted capacities, per test purlin

groups.description: Single-span, simply supported C- and Z-purlin roof assemblies with conventional through-fastened panels, loaded to failure downward (concrete blocks or vacuum chamber), each reporting a failure load per purlin and an AISI constrained-bending prediction.

constants.evidence: Table S1 header note: 'Purlins were spaced 5 ft. 0 in. on center (tributary width 5 ft.)'

members.note: Seven simulated gravity tests (Tests 1-6 and 16). Reported failure loads include the dead load carried by a test purlin, unlike most other papers. yield_stress_ksi is taken from the east test purlin; the west value is in a separate column of the same table.

groups.name: Single-span through-fastened purlin roof assemblies under gravity loading

groups.description: Full-scale multi-span continuous purlin roof assemblies with lapped purlins over the interior supports, loaded downward to failure (vacuum chamber or simulated gravity), reporting a failure load per purlin line for the continuous system.

members.note: Nine three-span confirming tests (test_id ending -3). The Table 2.1 join is by test set prefix (e.g. 'Z-R-R/S' serving 'Z-R-R/S-3') and supplies purlin_orientation and the interior-support lap length. Tests Z-R-R/S-3 and Z-T-P/S-3 failed prematurely (shipping damage; brace connection failure) and were excluded by the authors.

constants.evidence: Table S1 header note: 'purlins spaced 5 ft o.c. with 1 ft deck overhang each side'

members.note: Seven continuous tests (four at Virginia Tech, three at Ceco). Table 2.2 supplies total_lap_ft; Table 5.1 supplies se_in3 and the base-test R used for the standing seam cases. failure_load_as_printed is the APPLIED load only; total_load_incl_self_weight_plf carries the dead-load-inclusive value. test_to_predicted_ratio taken from the inflection-point-not-a-brace-point case.

Two three-span through-fastened tests (one Z, one C) with 'gravity' produced by vacuum. CRITICAL UNIT DIFFERENCE: failure_load_as_printed is in psf of roof area, not plf per purlin; failure_load_unit carries this and the values must NOT be averaged with plf rows without conversion. The Z result is limited by deck buckling rather than purlin strength.

Six three-span continuous lapped Z-purlin tests with screw-down panels (Almoney and Murray 1998). The printed failure load is 3.75 ft x pressure PLUS purlin self-weight (8 plf; 12 plf for FV20-3, doubled panel), so it is carried in total_load_incl_self_weight_plf, not failure_load_plf. FV20-4 pressure is printed 'approximate' with an inconsistent 5.0 psf/in. factor (kept as printed). FV20-1/-2 top flanges point out, the others in (per test sheets). thickness and yield are coupon values from the failed purlin; end and center bays are different sections. (hand edit 2026-11-10, Cris Moen review)

notes: The nine groups split the corpus first by test type (full-scale assembly, diaphragm component, coupon, computed section property) and, within full-scale tests, by load direction (gravity vs uplift), continuity (single span vs multi span) and panel restraint (through-fastened vs standing seam). These are the variables the reports themselves treat as defining distinct populations, so rows from different groups should never be averaged together.

UNIT TRAP: failure loads are plf per purlin line in every paper except MBMA_7501 and MBMA_7506 (psf of roof area) and the 7501 values are approximate text ('about 40'). The failure_load_unit column is carried in every group so the program can refuse to mix them. Failure moments are kip-in in 8903/9002/9804/9906 but ft-lb in 8802; failure_moment_unit is likewise carried.

DEAD LOAD TRAP: what the 'failure load' includes differs by report. MBMA_9906 and MBMA_8404 explicitly include deck and purlin self weight; MBMA_9804 reports applied load only (total carried separately); MBMA_8201, MBMA_8302 and MBMA_8002 state that dead load is excluded or do not say. Any cross-paper strength comparison should flag this.

The base-test reduction factor is reported as a fraction in MBMA_9906 and MBMA_9804 (r_value, r) but as a percentage in MBMA_9002 (r_percent); two separate canonical variables are used and a divide-by-100 derivation links them.

Radius numbering is inconsistent between reports: MBMA_8201 uses r3 = bottom lip-to-flange and r4 = bottom flange-to-web, while MBMA_8302 and MBMA_8404 use the reverse. The cross-section group maps by physical meaning, following the harmonized definitions, not by symbol number.

MBMA_8404 reports yield stress separately for the east and west test purlins; the strength groups carry the east value as yield_stress_ksi. The west value remains available in the coupon group, which keeps one row per coupon.

Several papers print ratios in parentheses ('(0.96)') or with stray characters, and the 1975 appendices contain unreadable-character markers '[?]'. The program must treat any cell containing '[?]', 'NA' or a dash as missing rather than coercing it to a number.

The MBMA_8302 rotational restraint F-test (one digitized curve) and the MBMA_8201/MBMA_7501 fastener shear and screw pull-over component tests are single-source data with no second contributor, so no group is defined for them; they are retained only as companion information in the source tables.

The 1975 instrumentation appendices (MBMA_7501 strain/rotation tables, MBMA_7506 sensor tables) are load-increment time histories, not specimen-level results, and are deliberately excluded from all groups; only their Table S1 strength rows are pooled.

failure_load_psf: MBMA_7501 and MBMA_7506 print failure loads in psf of roof area, with no tributary width to convert to plf; they are carried in their own column, not in failure_load_plf (edited by hand 2026-11-04). MBMA_7501 dead load is in psf and is carried as deck_dead_load_psf (the canonical dead-load variable is plf).

Hand edit 2026-11-05 (Cris Moen): the database is limited to pressure (vacuum) box tests. MBMA_8002, MBMA_8201, MBMA_8302 and MBMA_8802 (concrete-block loading) are excluded in selection.csv; their members were removed from this plan, and the cantilever_diaphragm_tests and service_response_at_165plf groups, which came only from MBMA_8201/8302, were removed. Notes that still name these papers describe the reports for context only. Unit-label columns renamed load_unit_as_printed / moment_unit_as_printed so their headers carry no unit suffix.

Load-direction filter (hand edit 2026-11-10, Cris Moen review): the 'uplift_purlin_assemblies' group (MBMA_8404 Tests 7-15, MBMA_7501) was removed from the gravity set. Those uplift tests are pooled once, in the uplift set; MBMA_7501 moved to the uplift selection.
MBMA_8404 Test 13 is dropped before harmonizing (authors call it invalid, p.34) (hand edit 2026-11-10, Cris Moen review).

Variable 'failure_pressure_in_h2o' renamed 'manometer_reading_at_failure_in_of_water' (hand edit 2026-11-10): the new concordance appended a wrong unit suffix to it ('failure_pressure_in_h2o_psf'); the values are inches of water.

MBMA_8309 and its group 'single_span_vacuum_moment_tests_gravity' removed (hand edit 2026-11-10): EXCLUDED 2026-11-10 (Cris Moen): edge-stiffener study on a narrow two-purlin specimen (purlins 18 in. apart under a 34 in. panel, Fig. 3 p.11); failure moments only, panel/fastening/bracing not described; not a roof-system test

purlin_orientation normalized to 'same direction' / 'opposed' (hand edit 2026-11-10, Cris Moen: orientation labels normalized to 'same direction' / 'opposed'). The printed wording is kept in purlin_orientation_as_printed; where the paper says which way the flanges of an opposed pair point, opposed_flange_direction holds 'in' (toward each other) or 'out'. Note MBMA_8404 'Facing' is opposed (flanges in) while MBMA_9001 'Facing' is same direction.
summary: Eleven MBMA cold-formed purlin test reports (1975-2000) were pooled into nine populations: full-scale roof assembly tests split by load direction, span continuity and panel restraint, plus the supporting component populations (tensile coupons, cantilever diaphragms, measured cross-sections, computed AISI section properties and service-level response at a common 165 plf load). Pooling is based on each report's own standardized strength-summary table (Table S1) and on the physical test type, so that, for example, single-span standing seam base tests are never mixed with multi-span lapped continuous systems or with uplift tests.
